scenes.title: Managed Streaming (Kinesis, Pub/Sub)
scenes.narration: Managed streaming services like Amazon Kinesis and Google Pub/Sub ingest and deliver continuous event data reliably without you running any message brokers.

scenes.title: What Streaming Buys You
bullets: Producers publish events continuously and consumers read them in near real time.
The service durably buffers data so slow or offline consumers never lose events.
It scales throughput up and down without you provisioning or patching brokers.
scenes.narration: Streaming platforms let producers emit a constant flow of events that consumers process almost immediately. The service durably retains those events for a window, so a lagging consumer can catch up without data loss. Because it is managed, throughput scales elastically and you never patch a broker yourself.

scenes.title: A Streaming Pipeline
steps: Consumers read in order per shard
scenes.narration: A typical pipeline starts with producers pushing events into the stream. The service partitions data into shards and buffers it durably for a retention window. Consumers read each shard in order and, after processing, write results to storage or a warehouse. This decoupling lets producers and consumers scale independently.

scenes.title: Batch vs. Streaming
scenes.narration: Batch pipelines run on a schedule and accept higher latency in exchange for simplicity. Streaming pipelines process events continuously for near real-time results and naturally handle unbounded data. Choose streaming when freshness matters and batch when periodic updates are enough.

scenes.title: Publishing to Kinesis with boto3
scenes.code:
import boto3, json

kinesis = boto3.client("kinesis")
event = {"user_id": 42, "action": "click"}

kinesis.put_record(
    StreamName="clickstream",
    Data=json.dumps(event),
    PartitionKey=str(event["user_id"]),
)
scenes.narration: Publishing to a stream in Python is concise with boto3. You serialize the event to JSON and call put_record with the target stream. The partition key, here the user id, controls which shard the record lands on, which keeps all events for one user ordered and evenly distributes load across shards.

scenes.text: Managed streaming decouples producers from consumers with a durable, scalable buffer — reach for it whenever data freshness and continuous processing matter.
scenes.narration: Managed streaming services give you a durable, elastic buffer that separates producers from consumers. Whenever low latency and continuous processing matter, they let you build real-time pipelines without operating brokers.
